newsitem.title: INDIA: INDIAN HEADLINE STOCKS-Factors to watch-April 10.
newsitem.headline: INDIAN HEADLINE STOCKS-Factors to watch-April 10.

text.p: Following are some of the main factors affecting Indian stock markets on Thursday morning:
NEWS OUTLOOK:
** India's ruling coalition says on Wednesday make-or-break talks with rebellious Congress party to save Prime Minister H. D. Deve Gowda's ten-month-old government may not succeed

** "My prognosis is I don't think the talks will succeed, not in the second round, not in the third round," a senior alliance official tells reporters after leaders adjourn for the night after a first round of formal talks
** The second round of negotiations is due to begin this morning

** The United Front could dissolve parliament on April 11 if it becomes clear that the Congress and main opposition member Bharatiya Janata Party will vote against the coalition, the Times of India newspaper says
** Truck owners agree to end a 10-day strike that hit the economy and pushed up prices following an accord to bring back 2.2 million vehicles on the roads, a senior government official says
** Times of India newspaper says truck strike will continue in Maharashtra state unless chief minister gives a written assurance that the motor vehicle tax will be reduced

** Indian shares -- which surged nearly four percent on Wednesday on hopes the political crisis would see a speedy resolution -- are likely to fall back on the latest political developments, traders say
** Bankers say they expect the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) to announce a cut in deposit interest rates to enable banks to reduce lending rates and boost sagging industrial production

The RBI is due to issue its half-yearly credit policy statement on April 15. Current RBI rules allow banks to offer a maximum of 10 percent per annum for deposits with maturities up to one year. Bankers expect a reduction to around 9.0 percent
** RBI relaxes procedures on share purchases by expatriate Indians
"Indian companies will no longer have to approach the RBI twice for seeking permission for issue and export of shares to non-resident Indian investors (NRIs)," the central bank says
** Largest private private aluminium maker Hindalco says it expects a marginal decline in its 1996/97 (April-March) net profit due to power problems and low global aluminium prices
Hindalco says aluminium output in 1996/97 is expected to fall to around 167,000 tonnes from 175,398 tonnes in 1995/96
It says alumina output will also fall below the previous year. "We anticipate alumina production to be close to 330,000 MT in 1996/97 as compared to 341,000 MT in the previous year"
** Pharmaceuticals firm Ranbaxy Laboratories is due to announce its results for 1996/97 (April-March) later in the day
MARKETS:
** Bombay's benchmark index .BSESN surges 130.39 points, or 3.7 percent, to 3650.88 on Wednesday as coalition begins formal talks with erstwhile Congress ally
** The National Stock Exchange index .NSEI jumps four pct to 1,030.30
** Delhi share index gains 13.12 points to 766.52, Calcutta gains 1.64 points to 101.65 and Madras 86.72 points to 3,515.98
** Indian rupee INR= opens steady at 35.84/85 against the dollar
-- Bombay newsroom +91-22-265 9000
